newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN SUFFER SECOND DEFEAT IN FOUR DAYS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN SUFFER SECOND DEFEAT IN FOUR DAYS.

text.p: Bayern Munich's championship campaign appeared to be coming off the rails on Wednesday as a 2-0 defeat at promoted Arminia Bielefeld -- their second loss in four days -- handed the Bundesliga initiative to Borussia Dortmund.
Bayern's second defeat in four days allowed Dortmund to open a three-point lead courtesy of a 3-0 win over Hansa Rostock.
The Bavarians had lost just once in 20 matches all season before their calamitous 5-2 defeat at Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday, a result which allowed reigning champions Dortmund to take over top spot.
And on Wednesday two first-half goals from German international striker Stefan Kuntz helped middle-of-the-table Bielefeld sink a weak Bayern again.
European Cup quarter-finalists Dortmund's home victory over Rostock saw former German international striker Karlheinz Riedle scoring twice.
In the second surprise of the evening fourth-placed Leverkusen were unable to match their weekend form and lost 3-0 at 1860 Munich.
